title: Leadville Trail 100 Run — official event page (2027 entry, course, aid, cutoffs, crew, pacer, drop bags, weather)
claims: The 2027 Life Time Leadville Trail 100 Run presented by La Sportiva is scheduled for August 21, 2027.
The 2027 lottery opens December 1, 2026 and closes December 15, 2026; results are announced January 6, 2027.
Minimum participation age is 18+ on race day; the Leadville Trail 100 Run entry price is $495.
The race was first held in 1983, created by local miner Ken Chlouber after the closure of the Climax Mine; 45 runners started the first edition; 2023 marked the 40th anniversary.

The course is an out-and-back that starts and finishes in Leadville; it starts at 10,200 feet and climbs to Hope Pass at 12,500 feet with two Hope Pass crossings; the general course description states over 15,000 feet of elevation gain.

The 2026 edition used a Willow Fire reroute: runners headed west from Harrison Ave around Turquoise Lake and back east around the lake to avoid Willow Fire areas, rejoining the traditional course into Outward Bound; Hagerman Pass Road, Sugarloaf Mountain and Powerline were not featured.
The 2026 Willow Fire reroute measured 99.7 miles with 13,357 feet of elevation gain.

The current aid-station list has twelve stations: Carter Summit Mini Aid outbound mile 10.6; Turquoise Lake Dam outbound 20.5; Outward Bound outbound 26; Half Pipe outbound 31.8; Twin Lakes Village outbound 40.3; Hope Pass outbound 45.4; Winfield turnaround 52.2; Hope Pass inbound 59; Twin Lakes Village inbound 64; Half Pipe inbound 72.6; Outward Bound inbound 78.3; Turquoise Lake Dam inbound 84.2; Carter Summit is a limited hydration/nutrition mini aid.
Current outbound cutoffs: Turquoise Lake Dam 10:15am; Outward Bound 11:15am; Half Pipe 12:15pm; Twin Lakes Village 2:15pm; Hope Pass 4:45pm; Winfield 6:50pm.
Current inbound cutoffs: Twin Lakes Village 11:00pm; Half Pipe 2:00am Sunday; Outward Bound 3:45am Sunday; Turquoise Lake Dam 5:30am Sunday.
Big buckle cutoff is sub-25 hours; small buckle and official course cutoff is sub-30 hours; buckle eligibility uses chip time while course cutoffs use gun time.

There are three official crewing locations, each hit twice: Outward Bound (26 outbound / 78.3 inbound), Pipeline Alternate (29.6 outbound / 74.9 inbound), Twin Lakes Village (40.3 outbound / 64 inbound); crewing outside these locations disqualifies the runner; Twin Lakes Village is shuttle-only from Outward Bound.

Pacers may join beginning at Twin Lakes inbound (mile 61.8 in the pacer rules, mile 64 in the pacer transportation note); runners may use as many pacers as wished but only one at a time until mile 99; two pacer bibs are issued at packet pickup; pacers must sign a waiver and wear a bib at all times, may carry food and equipment as burros, and may not push, pull, carry or tow the runner, use a vehicle or bicycle, or take aid outside official locations.

Drop bags are accepted at five locations: Turquoise Dam, Outward Bound, Half Pipe, Twin Lakes and Winfield; bags must be clear plastic, labeled in large letters with bib number, name and aid station; liquids must be leak-proof in non-breakable containers; drop-off is Friday 11:00am-5:00pm at 316 Harrison Ave; return Sunday about 8:00am-5:00pm at the same store; unclaimed bags are donated.

Packet pickup is Friday 11:00am-5:00pm at 135 E 6th Street with photo ID, in person only; the mandatory athlete meeting is Friday 10:00am at Lake County High School Football Field; the start/finish is the corner of 6th St and Harrison; the starting line opens 3:00-3:45am and the race starts at 4:00am Saturday.

Athletes must park at Rodeo Grounds/Community Fields, Lake County Intermediate School or Lake County High School and take a shuttle or walk to the start; race-morning shuttles run 3:00-4:30am; post-race shuttles run Saturday 10:00pm-Sunday 10:30am.

August Leadville temperatures range from daytime highs in the upper 70s to nighttime lows in the upper 20s; mornings are sunny with afternoon showers; rain, hail and even snow are possible; lightning is hazardous above timberline; hypothermia can result from falling temperature, wind and precipitation and can be deadly; runners should not attempt the Hope Pass round trip without adequate warm and protective clothing because the summit is over 12,000 feet.
The operation is conducted on public lands under a special permit from the U.S. Bureau of Land Management and held on the San Isabel National Forest under a special use permit.

The awards ceremony is Sunday 12:00pm at Lake County High School Football Field; buckles are distributed in the finish chute; finisher hoodies are mailed; runners must finish under 30 hours to be official finishers.
Athletes cut off at Winfield are shuttled to Twin Lakes Village; there is no shuttle from Winfield directly back to Leadville; cell service returns once past Granite on the ride back.
The event page links Ride with GPS and Garmin Connect course entries for navigation; at verification time the 2027 course was still marked 'stay tuned'.
